lesson_title: Half the Oranges, Forever: Series and Sigma Notation
hook_text: Take half the bag. Then half of what's left. Forever. How much do you end up with? Infinity has an exact answer.
clip_script: A bag holds 16 oranges. Someone takes half: 8. Then half of what remains: 4. Then 2, then 1, then half an orange — forever. Add up everything ever taken. Infinitely many takings, so the total should be infinite, right? Wrong. There was only ever ONE bag. The total can never pass 16 — and it creeps as close to 16 as you like. So the infinite sum is EXACTLY 16. That is a convergent geometric series: each taking is the last one times a half, and whenever the ratio sits strictly between minus one and one, forever adds up to a number: a over one minus r. Eight over a half — sixteen. And here's the part already living in your calculator. Zero comma five five five repeating? That's takings of five tenths, five hundredths, five thousandths — ratio one tenth. Sum: five ninths. Type 5 divided by 9 and watch the fives march. Every repeating decimal is an infinite series that finished converging before you were born.
visual_style: An orange bag emptying in halving scoops, a running-total bar creeping toward a bold 16 line without touching it, then a calculator screen filling with 0,5555 and morphing into the fraction five ninths.
pacing: Rhythmic halvings, a suspended beat on the question, brisk snap into the calculator reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make infinity add up to an exact number.
